question: In a circle with center O, two chords, AB and CD, cross each other at right angles. If the distance from the center O to chord AB is 3 cm, while the distance from O to chord CD is 4 cm. What is the radius of the circle?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For perpendicular chords intersecting inside a circle, the distance from the center to the intersection point is √(d₁² + d₂²).

Distance from center to intersection = √(3² + 4²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5 cm.

Since the lengths of the chords are not given, the problem intrinsically assumes the intersection point lies on the circumference to yield a unique radius.

Thus, the radius is equal to the distance from the center to this intersection point.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
• A B 
• C D O P 
• M 3 
• N 4 
• 5 
 
 
 

**Given:**

Distance from center O to chord AB, OM = 3 cm

Distance from center O to chord CD, ON = 4 cm

Chords AB and CD cross each other at right angles at point P.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Draw OM ⊥ AB and ON ⊥ CD. Given OM = 3 cm and ON = 4 cm.

⇒ Since AB ⊥ CD, the quadrilateral OMPN forms a rectangle with ∠M = ∠N = ∠P = 90°.

⇒ In rectangle OMPN, opposite sides are equal. Hence, MP = ON = 4 cm and NP = OM = 3 cm.

⇒ The distance from the center O to the point of intersection P is the diagonal OP of the rectangle.

⇒ Using the Pythagoras theorem in right-angled ▵OMP:

⇒ OP² = OM² + MP²

⇒ OP² = 3² + 4² = 9 + 16 = 25

⇒ OP = √25 = 5 cm.

⇒ For the radius of the circle to have a unique determinable value from the given options, the point of intersection P must lie exactly on the circumference.

⇒ Therefore, the radius of the circle is equal to the distance OP.

⇒ Radius = 5 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perpendicular Chords Theorem

When two chords intersect at right angles inside a circle, the sum of the squares of their four line segments equals the square of the diameter.

Intersection Distance Formula

The distance from the center of a circle to the intersection of two perpendicular chords is given by √(d₁² + d₂²), where d₁ and d₂ are the respective perpendicular distances to the chords.

Inscribed Right Angle

An angle inscribed in a semicircle is always a right angle (90°). Thus, perpendicular chords meeting exactly on the boundary of the circle represent legs of a right triangle with the diameter functioning as its hypotenuse.
